title: Non-overlapped Frequency based Episode Significance under Markov Null Models

problem.claim: Frequent episode mining needs statistical significance assessment to identify important patterns in symbolic time series data.

gap.claim: Most available frequent episode mining methods support only iid null hypotheses, despite the desirability of modeling simple temporal dependencies.

contributions.claim: A method characterizes the distribution of non-overlapped episode occurrences for significance assessment under a Markovian null hypothesis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method's effectiveness is illustrated through simulations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frequent episode mining discovers temporal dependencies in symbolic time series.
Statistical significance testing is used to discard unimportant patterns.
Existing methods generally assume iid null models, although time-series data may require simple temporal dependencies.
The paper characterizes non-overlapped episode-occurrence distributions under a Markovian null hypothesis.
The authors report simulations illustrating the method's effectiveness.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact distribution characterization or testing procedure.
